sources.entry: KinetAios - Local-first multi-engine AI agent dashboard: run Claude Code, Codex, and a built-in ReAct engine side by side with shared cross-engine memory, MCP, and 40+ tools.

summary.one_liner: KinetAios is a local-first Electron desktop dashboard for running multiple AI agent sessions on Windows 11 and macOS, across a built-in ReAct engine, Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness.
summary.what_it_does: Runs many concurrent agent sessions with streaming answers, each with a selectable engine (Direct V1/V2/V3, Claude Code via the claude CLI, Codex via the codex CLI, or DeepSeek Harness via the dsh CLI) and a per-session model. Provides 30+ built-in tools (shell with confirmation, file read/write/edit, grep, glob, web fetch and search, git diff, sub-agents, teams) plus native computer-use actions such as screenshots and mouse/keyboard control. Stores history in SQLite with FTS5 and extracts long-term facts about the user that are shared across engines and sessions. Acts as both an MCP client (auto-discovers configured servers) and an MCP server exposing a run_agent tool over HTTP+SSE. Includes a plugin SDK, pipelines that chain engines, session branching and export, a Git and file browser, and a global hotkey quick panel.
use_cases: run Claude Code and Codex agents side by side in one window
keep AI chat memory across sessions and engines on my own machine
automate shell, file editing and web research with an LLM agent
chain multiple AI engines into a pipeline
control a desktop with AI screenshots and mouse/keyboard actions
open a quick AI prompt panel with a global hotkey
notable: Four agent engines switchable per session, with Pipeline handoff of context between them
Long-term memory stored locally in SQLite and shared across all engines
Built-in MCP client and server (run_agent tool, token auth)
Native computer-use tools (screenshot, window capture, mouse, keyboard) on Windows and macOS
Plugin SDK with 20+ built-in plugins for tools, slash commands, hooks and panels
caveats: Global hotkey only works while the app is running; window close defaults to minimize
Windows installers must be built on Windows; cross-building from macOS is unreliable
Builds are unsigned by default, so SmartScreen and Gatekeeper warn until a signing cert and notarization are added
Requires your own LLM API key; the Claude Code and Codex engines depend on those CLIs being installed
